Rubric for the APM loop (Associate Product Manager), req REQ-2025-031. Third version. v1 was a disaster of gut feel, v2 was too long (7 interviews!). This one is 4 interviews plus a debrief.

## Why we bother

Last year we hired two people mostly because Henk liked them over lunch. One worked out. The point of the rubric: everyone scores the same things, writes notes before the debrief, and we don't anchor on whoever talks first.

## The loop

| # | Interview | Who | Length |
|---|-----------|-----|--------|
| 1 | Screen call | Yasmina | 30 min |
| 2 | Product sense | Priya | 60 min |
| 3 | Prioritisation case | Tomás + Sanne | 75 min |
| 4 | Stakeholder roleplay | Jens (on Zoom) | 45 min |
| 5 | Values chat | Henk | 30 min |

Target: whole loop done within 10 working days of the screen. In March we averaged 16. Not great.

## Scoring scale

1 = strong no, 2 = no, 3 = yes, 4 = strong yes. No 2.5, no "3 but". If you can't decide, it's a 2.

Every interviewer submits in Ashby within 24h, before seeing anyone else's score. Ashby hides the others until you submit, so no excuse.

## Product sense

The prompt we use: "A warehouse manager says trucks wait too long at the gate. What do you build?"

### What a 4 looks like

- Asks who is waiting: driver, carrier dispatcher, warehouse? Different problems.
- Gets to data: what's the wait now, where does the time go.
- Proposes something small first (a dock slot booking page) before a full optimiser.
- Mentions what they would not build.

### What a 2 looks like

- Jumps straight to "AI route optimisation".
- No numbers at all.
- Builds for the warehouse only, forgets carriers exist.

## Prioritisation case

Case CASE-RTD-04: "the Rotterdam cross-dock". 14 feature requests, 3 sprints of capacity, one angry customer (Waalhaven Koel BV) threatening to leave. They get the pack 48h before.

Good signals: makes trade-offs explicit, uses some kind of impact vs effort sort, says no to the angry customer on at least one thing and explains how they'd tell them. Red flag: tries to do all 14.

## Stakeholder roleplay

Jens plays an engineering lead who thinks the spec is nonsense. Script is in the shared drive (roleplay-jens-v2.docx). He's very convincing. Two people cried in v2, so we softened it: Jens now gives one opening for compromise at minute 20.

## Values chat

Henk only. Three questions, fixed:
1. Tell me about a time you were wrong and how you found out.
2. What do you do when your manager is wrong?
3. What's a product you think is badly designed and why?

## Debrief rules

- 30 min, max 2 days after the last interview.
- Lowest scorer speaks first. Then the highest.
- Hire needs: no 1s, at least two 4s, average of 3.0 or above.
- Henk has a veto but has to write down why. He's used it once (March 2025, candidate C-117).

## Results so far

Round in spring 2025: 41 CVs, 12 screens, 5 full loops, 1 offer. Lieke Jansen accepted 2 May, starts 2 June, see [[Onboarding checklist]]. Offer €52,000 + 8% holiday pay.
